- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or negative; adjust upward by 1–2% for short-term (1–7 day) forecasts.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model lags; forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- Mean reversion is overestimated in model; if price is above 3σ from 30-day mean, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 15–30 day forecasts, model tends to underestimate true price when sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6); apply +1–2% bias to align with sentiment-driven momentum.
